newInTask.title: Root mean squared error
newInTask.meaning: RMSE squares each aligned error, averages the squares and takes the square root. Larger misses have more influence and the result retains the target unit.

newInTask.title: pd.crosstab(..., normalize="index")
newInTask.meaning: Counts category pairs, then divides each row by its row total. Rows are island-specific proportions, not classification accuracy.

newInTask.title: Regularise the expanded model
newInTask.meaning: Ridge fits a linear prediction rule with a penalty on squared coefficients. PolynomialFeatures supplies its curved input terms; scaling those terms makes their penalties comparable.

visualTeaching.concept: Constrain the number of fitting rows in each leaf
visualTeaching.reason: The preceding task changes maximum depth. This task introduces minimum leaf support, so its control changes only min_samples_leaf on the same observations.

newInTask.title: Minimum leaf support
newInTask.meaning: min_samples_leaf requires each terminal leaf to contain at least this many fitting observations. Compare 1, 5 and 10 using the same training folds; larger values prevent tiny leaves.

newInTask.title: Inspect fitted pipeline steps
newInTask.meaning: The model step is the fitted classifier. Its coef_ rows belong to the supplied fitted class order, and columns follow the input feature order. Reading these coefficients does not fit the pipeline again.

visualTeaching.reason: This task first retrieves neighbour positions through fitted pipeline steps and counts their labels. The diagram fixes k at five and lets learners inspect those rows.

newInTask.title: Inspect fitted pipeline steps
newInTask.meaning: named_steps accesses the fitted steps by their authored names: scale standardises the query; model contains the five-neighbour classifier. Ordinary Pipeline.predict performs these steps automatically.

newInTask.title: Retrieve and count neighbour votes
newInTask.meaning: kneighbors returns positions in the fitted training table. Those positions select training labels whose votes determine the prediction; they are not positions in the test table.

newInTask.title: Inspect fitted pipeline steps
newInTask.meaning: The model step is the fitted SVM. Its n_support_ counts the support vectors for each class in model.classes_ order. Reading these counts does not fit the pipeline again.

newInTask.title: 1 - p_A**2 - p_B**2
newInTask.meaning: Gini is zero for a single-class node. Weight child impurities by their shares of the parent’s observations.

newInTask.title: np.exp(model.feature_log_prob_)
newInTask.meaning: BernoulliNB stores logarithms of fitted presence probabilities, in model.classes_ and input-feature order. exp reverses the logarithm; these are feature likelihoods, not posterior class probabilities.

newInTask.title: Deeper investigation: affine LDA scores
newInTask.meaning: For binary LDA with shared covariance, the signed log-odds score is affine: a feature midpoint has the average endpoint score. This identity does not apply to the nonlinear conversion into probabilities.

newInTask.title: MLPRegressor(hidden_layer_sizes=(8,))
newInTask.meaning: MLPRegressor configures a network for a numerical outcome. hidden_layer_sizes=(8,) keeps one eight-unit hidden layer; constructing the recipe does not fit its weights.

newInTask.title: DataFrame.diff()
newInTask.meaning: Subtracts the previous row from each numeric column. The initial change is missing because there is no previous row. Use the ordered budgets shown here.

newInTask.title: np.allclose(left, right)
newInTask.meaning: Returns one Boolean comparing aligned numeric values within a small floating-point tolerance. Compare arrays of the same shape here; equal shape alone does not imply equal coordinates or meaning.

newInTask.title: DataFrame.join(external_labels)
newInTask.meaning: Adds a labelled Series using matching row indices. The operation changes the displayed table, not the fitted PCA axes or coordinates.

newInTask.title: Typical absolute error
newInTask.meaning: MAE averages the magnitude of aligned errors, giving each extra target-unit miss the same weight. It answers a different error-cost question from RMSE.

newInTask.title: Average recall across classes
newInTask.meaning: Balanced accuracy averages the fraction of each class correctly recovered. Every class has equal weight; precision of an alert is a separate question.

newInTask.code: cv_results = {name: cross_validate(candidate, X_train, y_train, cv=folds, scoring=metric) for name, candidate in candidates.items()}
newInTask.title: Repeat a comparison across named candidates
newInTask.meaning: The dictionary comprehension repeats the same validation operation for each named recipe. items() supplies each name and estimator together; the result keeps the scores under that name.
